subject: giraffe
pitch: A young reticulated giraffe. Chestnut patches outlined by bright cream lines all over its body and neck, a short mane of stiff brown hair down the neck, two fuzzy ossicones with black tufts on top, big ears, long lashes, a long dark tongue just peeking out, and slender legs fading to cream above the hooves.
reasoning:

For the body parts, I'll rely on the confirmed APIs like part, sweep, spike, and stick rather than guessing at uncertain ones like rod or paint. For the giraffe's patches, I'm thinking of scattering flattened dodecahedron shapes across the surface with a cream outline underneath to mimic the coat pattern, oriented along the surface normal.

I'll just commit to Y-axis orientation for the bumps, scaling cream and brown icosahedra slightly differently so brown sits higher. For the torso, instead of a constant-radius sweep which looks dull, I'll shape it from a scaled sphere instead.

Legs are probably safer as sweeps along polylines (hip to knee to ankle) with hooves as dark boxes at the end, using brown-ish upper leg and cream lower leg coloring with patches. I'm setting up mirrored joint hierarchies for left/right sides, then moving to head details—jaw, upper skull/snout, a small dark tongue poking from the mouth, and lash spikes near each eye, with eye spheres positioned precisely on the face.
